story.title: Our Story
story.content: We connect farmers from the pristine mountains of Sankhuwasabha directly to your home. Our sweet, mineral-rich jaggery is made using traditional methods completely devoid of bleach or artificial coloring. By choosing SakharSansar, you are not only savoring an authentic taste but also supporting rural livelihoods.

farmers.name: Ram Bahadur
farmers.story: Farming sugarcane for 20 years, Ram uses organic techniques to produce the sweetest yields.

products.name: Sankhuwasabha Sakhar Block
products.description: Wood-fired Sankhuwasabha sakhar poured into rounds and left to set. Sold by the kilo, roughly three discs to a pack.
products.longDescription: This is the Sankhuwasabha sakhar everything else here is made from. Cane pressed in Sankhuwasabha, reduced over an open wood fire in an iron kadhai, skimmed by hand and poured into moulds while still molten. It sets overnight into dense amber discs, about three to the kilo, with the cracked surface and uneven colour that come from setting in open air rather than a machine. No sulphur, no clarifier, no colour, no added sugar. Break a piece into your chiya, grate it into what you are cooking, or eat a chip of it after a meal the way it has always been eaten in the hills.
products.metaDescription: Sankhuwasabha Sakhar (सखर) block, 1kg for Rs. 400. Wood-fired, poured by hand. No sulphur, no added sugar.
products.shelfLife: 6-12 months when stored in a cool, dry place
products.tastingNotes: The densest thing we make. It chips rather than crumbles, breaking to a dark amber face that catches the light. Toasted molasses lands first, then a long mineral finish carrying the faint smoke of the wood fire it was reduced over. This is the reference flavour — the powder is this block, crushed.
howToUse: Chip a thumbnail-sized piece straight into hot chiya and let it dissolve as you stir.
Grate over kheer, halwa or sel roti batter for a deeper, less sugary sweetness.
Melt with a splash of water into a pouring syrup for festival sweets.
Keep a small piece to eat after a heavy meal, the way it has always been eaten in the hills.
products.sourcing: Cane is cut at first light and pressed within hours, before the juice can start to ferment. It is then reduced over open wood-fire in iron kadhais, skimmed by hand, and poured into moulds while still molten. Each disc rests overnight to set before it is wrapped.

faqs.q: How many pieces come in a kilo?
faqs.a: Usually three discs, sometimes four. They are poured by hand, so individual weights vary and the pack is made up to a kilo rather than to a fixed count.

faqs.q: How do I break up a disc?
faqs.a: Rest it on a board and tap along one edge with the back of a heavy knife or a rolling pin; it splits along its own grain. Do not try to cut straight down through the middle. Many people break a whole disc up once and keep the pieces in a jar.

faqs.q: Why is this batch darker than the last one I bought?
faqs.a: Colour shifts batch to batch with how late in the season the cane was cut and how long that particular kadhai ran. Darker generally means a longer reduction and a stronger molasses note. It is not a sign of age or of anything added.

faqs.q: Is this the same sakhar as the powder?
faqs.a: Yes. The Sakhar Powder is this block crushed and sieved. The block is the less processed of the two, and works out cheaper by weight.

products.name: Sankhuwasabha Sakhar Powder
products.description: Our Sankhuwasabha sakhar block, crushed and sieved to a free-flowing powder. Dissolves cold, measures like sugar.
products.longDescription: The same wood-fired Sankhuwasabha sakhar as our block, crushed once it has fully set and sieved to an even grain. It pours, it measures, and it dissolves without leaving anything at the bottom of the cup — hot or cold — which is what makes it the easy everyday swap for refined sugar. Spoon it into chiya, use it where a recipe asks for brown sugar, or sprinkle it over oats and curd with no melting step in between. Nothing is added at this stage: no anti-caking agent, no starch, no flour. The 250g pouch is resealable, which matters more than it sounds — loose sakhar pulls moisture out of the air within hours.
products.metaDescription: Sankhuwasabha Sakhar (सखर) powder, 250g for Rs. 149. Our wood-fired block, crushed and sieved. Dissolves cold.
products.shelfLife: 6 months when stored in an airtight container
products.tastingNotes: Lighter in the cup than the block it comes from — crushing exposes more surface, which softens the smoke and pushes the clean caramel forward. It dissolves without leaving a grain behind, hot or cold, which is exactly why it suits baking and cold drinks where the block never worked.
howToUse: Spoon straight into tea, coffee or lassi; it dissolves cold, unlike the block.
Swap it one-for-one where a recipe asks for brown sugar.
Sprinkle over oats, yoghurt or cut fruit without any melting step.
Whisk into marinades and glazes, where it browns faster than refined sugar.
products.sourcing: Made from our own Sakhar Block once it has fully set — crushed, then sieved to an even grain so it pours and measures consistently. Nothing is added at this stage: no anti-caking agent, no starch, no flour. It is packed straight into a resealable pouch, because loose sakhar pulls moisture out of the air within hours.

faqs.q: Can I substitute it one-for-one for sugar in baking?
faqs.a: For brown sugar, yes, measure for measure. For white sugar, start at about three-quarters of the amount — sakhar reads sweeter and browns faster, so also check your bake a few minutes early.

faqs.q: My powder has clumped into a solid lump. Is it spoiled?
faqs.a: No. Sakhar powder is hygroscopic, so it draws in humidity and cakes, which is common in Kathmandu through the monsoon. Break it up with a fork or a short pulse in a grinder and keep the pouch properly sealed; the flavour is unaffected.

faqs.q: Why choose the powder over the block?
faqs.a: Convenience and cold solubility. The block keeps longer, has a slightly stronger smoke and costs less by weight, but it has to be chipped or grated and it will not dissolve in a cold drink. If you sweeten daily, most people find the powder easier.

products.name: Mixed Dry Fruits
products.description: Mixed nuts turned through our own wood-fired Sankhuwasabha sakhar and left to set. A snack, not a sweet.
products.longDescription: Whole dry fruits, warmed and turned through molten sakhar until each one carries a thin, matte coat, then spread out to cool loose rather than pressed into a slab. The sakhar is the same wood-fired batch that goes into our blocks, which is why the coating tastes of toasted molasses rather than plain sugar. Nuts stay crisp underneath. There is no glucose syrup, no colour and no flavouring in it — the pieces look uneven and slightly dusty because that is what setting sakhar does when nothing is added to keep it glossy. A 100g pouch is about a week of afternoons.
products.metaDescription: Whole nuts turned through molten Sankhuwasabha sakhar. No glucose syrup, no colour. 100g pouch for Rs. 299.
products.ingredients: Mixed dry fruits, pure sugarcane sakhar
products.shelfLife: 3 months in a sealed pouch, kept cool and dry
products.tastingNotes: The coating goes first — toasted molasses, a little smoke, gone in a couple of seconds — and then you are left chewing the nut itself, which is the point. Far less sweet than a chikki, because the sakhar is a thin shell rather than a slab holding everything together. Each piece tastes slightly different depending on what is under it.
howToUse: Eat a small handful in the afternoon instead of a biscuit.
Scatter over curd, kheer or ice cream for crunch and a little sweetness.
Pack a pouch for a trek or a long bus journey; it keeps better than anything with cream in it.
Set a bowl out with tea when people come over.
products.sourcing: Dry fruits are sorted by hand, then turned through sakhar melted from the same wood-fired batch we mould our blocks from. They are spread to cool in a single layer so the pieces stay separate instead of setting into a sheet. Nothing else goes in — no glucose syrup, no colour, no flavouring, no preservative — which is why the shelf life is shorter than for the plain sakhar.

faqs.a: Much less than a chikki or a sugar-coated nut. The sakhar is a thin shell, not a binder, so most of what you are eating is the dry fruit itself. People who find traditional sweets too much usually get on with this.

faqs.q: Why do the pieces look dull rather than glossy?
faqs.a: Setting sakhar dries to a matte, slightly powdery finish on its own. A glossy coat needs glucose syrup or a glazing agent, and neither goes into this. The dusty look is the honest one.

faqs.q: Will it stick together in warm weather?
faqs.a: The coating softens above roughly 30°C and pieces can tack together in the pouch. They separate with a light tap and the taste is unaffected. Keep it out of direct sun, and in peak summer the fridge does no harm.
Yes — it is a dry fruit and nut mix, so it is not suitable for anyone with a nut allergy. Message us before ordering if you need the exact composition of the current batch.

faqs.question: How is your jaggery different from market jaggery?
faqs.answer: Our jaggery is 100% chemical-free. We do not use sulfur, bleach, or synthetic colors during the boiling process, ensuring you get the pure sugarcane extract in its most natural form.

faqs.question: What is the shelf life of the jaggery?
faqs.answer: Store it in a cool, dark, and dry place in an airtight container. Properly preserved, it can easily last 6-12 months without losing its flavor or nutritional value.

faqs.question: Can diabetic patients consume jaggery?
faqs.answer: While healthier and more nutritious than refined sugar, jaggery is still a sweetener with a high glycemic index. We recommend diabetic individuals consult their physician before adding it to their diet.

faqs.question: Do you deliver pan-Nepal?
faqs.answer: Yes! We ship directly from Sankhuwasabha to major cities across Nepal. Shipping times vary depending on your location.
